label: prf:groebner-shirshov-energy
title: Proof of groebner shirshov energy
html:
Proof. Proof of groebner shirshov energy

Proof.

Part 1. The Yang--Baxter relation \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} has the same word length on both sides (\ell = 3) and coefficient 1. Applying it to a term c \cdot w produces c \cdot w' where |c| = |c| and \ell(w') = \ell(w). The same holds for far commutativity. Only the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 \mapsto (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 changes the word length (from \ell to \ell - 1) and splits one coefficient into two.

Part 2. The Gröbner--Shirshov basis G satisfies the Bergman diamond lemma (the main theorem of the Gröbner--Shirshov basis theory, main theorem). For any two overlapping reductions, the results can be further reduced to the same normal form. Because the energy is computed from the unique normal form, the energy is path-independent.

Part 3. Let c \cdot \sigma_i^2 \cdot (\text{suffix}) be a reducible term. After applying the Hecke relation:

  • One term has coefficient c(q - q^{-1}) and word length \ell - 1 (the \sigma_i term).
  • One term has coefficient c and word length \ell - 2 (the identity term). The total weight changes by |c(q-q^{-1})| + |c| - |c| = |c| \cdot |q - q^{-1}|.

Substrate-internal: GS reduction over the Habiro embedding. The reduction rules in G (Hecke, Yang–Baxter, far commutativity) act strictly within the polynomial embedding \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] \hookrightarrow \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} (Habiro ring). Confluence (the Bergman diamond lemma) is an exact algebraic consequence of the foundational triple (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). It holds in any base ring where the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 applies. In particular, it holds over the motivic substrate before any place-realization. The energy functional E(\xi) takes values in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[q^{\pm 1}] as a formal Laurent polynomial. Its evaluation as a real-valued physical quantity (Skein binding energy) requires the archimedean realization \rho_\infty (archimedean realization) of the substrate. This occurs downstream of the reduction itself.
